Summary

Add the /chronicle command family (standup, search, tips, cost-tips, improve, reindex) to the Agent Host so users can invoke session history insights directly from VS Code chat.

 Motivation

The /chronicle commands provide powerful session history analysis (standup reports, usage tips, cost optimization, workflow improvements) via the session_store_sql tool. These are currently available through the CLI but not surfaced in VS Code's Agent Host. Users should be able to access these from the same chat surface where they do their work.

 Subcommands

| Subcommand | Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|
| standup | agent-prompt | Get a report on your work from the last day |
| search | agent-prompt | Search all session content by keyword or topic |
| tips | agent-prompt | Get personalized tips based on usage patterns |
| cost-tips | agent-prompt | Get tips to reduce token usage and cost |
| improve | agent-prompt | Suggest improvements to copilot-instructions.md |
| reindex | local (no model) | Rebuild the session store index |

 Implementation Plan

 Phase 1: Completion Provider (discoverability)

1. Extend CopilotSlashCommandName in copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts — add 'chronicle' to the type union, COMMANDS array, and getCommandDescription(). Insert text should be /chronicle (trailing space to prompt subcommand entry).

2. Add chronicle subcommand completions — detect /chronicle prefix and offer sub-completions for the 6 subcommands. Either extend the existing provider or create a dedicated provider.

3. Update parseLeadingSlashCommand() regex to recognize /chronicle followed by optional subcommand + remaining text.

 Phase 2: Command Execution (send handler)

4. Add chronicle dispatch in CopilotAgentSession.send() — parse subcommand from slashCommand.rest, build the agent prompt, inject as message text. For reindex: complete turn locally (like /compact).

5. Create chroniclePrompts.ts — new file at src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/chroniclePrompts.ts with prompt builders for each subcommand (standup, search, tips, cost-tips, improve). Each prompt instructs the model to use session_store_sql with the appropriate schema.

 Phase 3: Tool & Store Availability

6. Ensure session_store_sql is available — verify the tool is registered for agent host sessions when chronicle prompts are injected. The tool needs access to the session store (cloud DuckDB or local SQLite).

 Phase 4: Feature Gating

7. Add config/feature flag — gate behind a config key (similar to AgentHostConfigKey.RubberDuck). Hide from completions when disabled or when no session store is available.

 Relevant Files

- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts — command list, type, regex
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts — send() dispatch
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/chroniclePrompts.ts — new, prompt builders
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts — provider registration
- extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/common/toolNames.ts — already has SessionStoreSql
- extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts — session store writer (reference)

 Design Decisions

- Prompt injection pattern: Same approach as /plan, /research, /rubber-duck — rewrite prompt text in send() before forwarding to the SDK.
- Cloud vs. local store: Target cloud session store (DuckDB syntax) since the agent host is connected to GitHub. Fall back to local SQLite if cloud is unavailable.
- Subcommand completion UX: Space-separated form (/chronicle standup) matching existing parser behavior.
- reindex handling: Complete turn locally (like /compact) since it's a side-effect, not a model interaction.
- /chronicle search without query: Return inline help text rather than invoking the model.

 Verification

1. Type / → chronicle appears in completion list with description
2. Type /chronicle → subcommand completions appear
3. Submit /chronicle standup → model receives prompt and uses session_store_sql
4. Submit /chronicle reindex → completes locally without model
5. Feature flag off → command hidden from completions and rejected in send
6. Unit tests for command parsing and prompt generation
kept_issues.body:
## Summary

Add the `/chronicle` command family (standup, search, tips, cost-tips, improve, reindex) to the Agent Host so users can invoke session history insights directly from VS Code chat.

## Motivation

The `/chronicle` commands provide powerful session history analysis (standup reports, usage tips, cost optimization, workflow improvements) via the `session_store_sql` tool. These are currently available through the CLI but not surfaced in VS Code's Agent Host. Users should be able to access these from the same chat surface where they do their work.

## Subcommands

| Subcommand | Behavior | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `standup` | agent-prompt | Get a report on your work from the last day |
| `search <query>` | agent-prompt | Search all session content by keyword or topic |
| `tips` | agent-prompt | Get personalized tips based on usage patterns |
| `cost-tips` | agent-prompt | Get tips to reduce token usage and cost |
| `improve` | agent-prompt | Suggest improvements to copilot-instructions.md |
| `reindex` | local (no model) | Rebuild the session store index |

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Completion Provider (discoverability)

1. **Extend `CopilotSlashCommandName`** in `copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts` — add `'chronicle'` to the type union, `COMMANDS` array, and `getCommandDescription()`. Insert text should be `/chronicle ` (trailing space to prompt subcommand entry).

2. **Add chronicle subcommand completions** — detect `/chronicle ` prefix and offer sub-completions for the 6 subcommands. Either extend the existing provider or create a dedicated provider.

3. **Update `parseLeadingSlashCommand()` regex** to recognize `/chronicle` followed by optional subcommand + remaining text.

### Phase 2: Command Execution (send handler)

4. **Add chronicle dispatch in `CopilotAgentSession.send()`** — parse subcommand from `slashCommand.rest`, build the agent prompt, inject as message text. For `reindex`: complete turn locally (like `/compact`).

5. **Create `chroniclePrompts.ts`** — new file at `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/chroniclePrompts.ts` with prompt builders for each subcommand (standup, search, tips, cost-tips, improve). Each prompt instructs the model to use `session_store_sql` with the appropriate schema.

### Phase 3: Tool & Store Availability

6. **Ensure `session_store_sql` is available** — verify the tool is registered for agent host sessions when chronicle prompts are injected. The tool needs access to the session store (cloud DuckDB or local SQLite).

### Phase 4: Feature Gating

7. **Add config/feature flag** — gate behind a config key (similar to `AgentHostConfigKey.RubberDuck`). Hide from completions when disabled or when no session store is available.

## Relevant Files

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts` — command list, type, regex
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts` — `send()` dispatch
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/chroniclePrompts.ts` — **new**, prompt builders
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts` — provider registration
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/common/toolNames.ts` — already has `SessionStoreSql`
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chronicle/vscode-node/sessionStoreTracker.ts` — session store writer (reference)

## Design Decisions

- **Prompt injection pattern**: Same approach as `/plan`, `/research`, `/rubber-duck` — rewrite prompt text in `send()` before forwarding to the SDK.
- **Cloud vs. local store**: Target cloud session store (DuckDB syntax) since the agent host is connected to GitHub. Fall back to local SQLite if cloud is unavailable.
- **Subcommand completion UX**: Space-separated form (`/chronicle standup`) matching existing parser behavior.
- **`reindex` handling**: Complete turn locally (like `/compact`) since it's a side-effect, not a model interaction.
- **`/chronicle search` without query**: Return inline help text rather than invoking the model.

## Verification

1. Type `/` → chronicle appears in completion list with description
2. Type `/chronicle ` → subcommand completions appear
3. Submit `/chronicle standup` → model receives prompt and uses `session_store_sql`
4. Submit `/chronicle reindex` → completes locally without model
5. Feature flag off → command hidden from completions and rejected in send
6. Unit tests for command parsing and prompt generation
kept_issues.title: Add /chronicle command set to Agent Host

kept_issues._normalized_body:
The chat feature currently uses the term "todos" (e.g. the todo list / todo tool). The word "todos" is ambiguous because it is also a Spanish word ("todos" = "all/everyone") and is read/pronounced that way, which can be confusing — especially for screen reader users and non-English speakers.

 Proposal
Rename "todos" to "tasks" throughout the chat experience for clarity.

 Areas to update
- UI labels and strings (localized)
- Setting IDs / keys (with backward-compat aliases where needed)
- Command IDs and titles
- Tool name / tool reference name (preserve backward compatibility via legacy names)
- ARIA labels and accessibility help text
- Documentation

 Notes
- Tool/command/setting renames must keep backward compatibility (legacy aliases) so existing references keep working.

my request is comade with copilot since im not a native english speaker:

Dear Microsoft / VS Code team,
I would like to suggest adding a dedicated "Restart VS Code" button to the user interface.
Currently, VS Code prompts users to restart after updates, but there is no easy, always-available way to manually trigger a full restart when needed. Having a restart option would be useful in cases where users want to ensure that the session is fully reset (e.g., after changing settings, extensions, or troubleshooting issues).
Proposed solution

Add a "Restart VS Code" button accessible from the UI
A natural location could be under the Settings gear menu or the Command Palette
The action should:

Fully restart the application
Preserve workspace state similar to normal restarts

Why this would be helpful

Ensures a clean session without leftover state
Improves troubleshooting experience
Provides consistency (restart is already prompted after updates)
Makes the feature more discoverable for users who are not familiar with command-based workflows

Additional context
This is a small quality-of-life improvement, but it would be a nice and practical addition to the overall developer experience.

Description
I often find the placement of arrow keys on laptops quite uncomfortable, especially while coding. A typical scenario is when I’m typing a variable name and VS Code auto-completes it with a semicolon. Everything looks fine until I realise I need to move to the next line to continue typing.
At that point, I have to lift my hand, locate the awkwardly positioned arrow keys, and use them to navigate—only to repeat this process again and again. It feels like an unnecessary interruption to the typing flow and overall productivity.
I believe this is a common annoyance, and I’d be interested to know if others have experienced the same or found better solutions.
One workaround I’ve tried is using Ctrl + Enter, which inserts a new line and moves the cursor to it. However, this approach is not very effective when there is existing code on the next line that needs to be edited, so it’s not suitable in many situations.
I also attempted remapping keys on my laptop, but the alternative keys available for remapping are themselves not ergonomically placed, so this didn’t help much.
I’m reaching out to the VS Code team and the community for suggestions or best practices to address this issue. Ideally, I’d like to avoid purchasing and carrying an external keyboard, especially given my hybrid work setup.

If nothing already exist to tackle this issue then could you look at this as a feature request?

VSCode v1.123 added a hard coded two hours delay for auto-updating extensions, but not for "trusted publishers" Microsoft, GitHub and Open AI.

 Note: This delay does not apply to extensions from trusted publishers such as Microsoft, GitHub, and OpenAI. These extensions continue to update immediately.

A PR for making this delay configurable was just merged: < 

An issue for making the cooldown setting apply to installs too was created: < 

But I see no issue about making the list of trusted publishers configurable too.

6. Rename a chat, then reload the Agents window — confirm the new name persists.

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Problem

There is no public Extension API to query whether the sidebar, panel (bottom), or auxiliary bar are currently visible. The internal IWorkbenchLayoutService has exactly what's needed — isVisible("workbench.parts.sidebar") and onDidChangePartVisibility — but neither is bridged to the extension host.

As a result, extensions that need to save and restore layout state (e.g. a "maximize editor" toggle) have no reliable way to read the current visibility of these three parts. The only workaround is to parse VS Code's internal SQLite database (state.vscdb) directly, which is fragile and reads stale data mid-session.

The layout buttons in the VS Code title bar already track this state correctly because they run in the renderer process with direct access to the layout service. Extensions cannot do the same.

 Proposed API

Add to vscode.window:

 

 Use Case

A "maximize editor" extension needs to:
1. Read current visibility of all three parts before hiding them
2. Restore only the parts that were originally visible

Without this API, if the user hides the bottom panel manually before pressing maximize, the extension has no way to know — and incorrectly restores it on unmaximize.

This is a general-purpose API gap: any extension that interacts with workbench layout (focus modes, presentation modes, Zen-like toggles) hits the same wall.

 Current Workaround (and why it's bad)

Read ~/.config/Code/User/workspaceStorage/ /state.vscdb directly via a custom SQLite B-tree parser. Problems:
- Only accurate at window open (VS Code flushes the DB on close, not on toggle)
- Relies on undocumented internal key names (workbench.sideBar.hidden, etc.)
- Breaks if VS Code changes its storage format

 Prior Art

- Context keys sideBarVisible, panelVisible, auxiliaryBarVisible already exist internally and are kept in sync via onDidChangePartVisibility
- These are used in when clauses in package.json but cannot be read at runtime by extension code
- Exposing them (or wrapping isVisible()) would be a small bridge with high utility
kept_issues.title: API: expose panel/sidebar/auxiliaryBar visibility state to extensions

Summary

The VS Code Terminal Shell Integration documentation currently lists the following supported shells:

 Linux/macOS: bash, fish, pwsh, zsh
 Windows: Git Bash, pwsh

tcsh (and its ancestor csh) are not supported.

This is a significant gap for users working in Hardware companies/EDA/HPC environments, academic institutions, and legacy Unix systems where tcsh is the default and often mandatory shell.

---

 The main issue

The lack of shell integration with tcsh/csh causing the agents to:
1. Do extra iterations when using shell tool (exec), using wrong syntax (EOF, 2>&1, multiline strings etc.)
2. Not communicate with the environment correctly - not knowing if command finished and the exit status
3. High token spending and high costs.

Summary

Add Multi-Chat support to the Claude harness so it matches the Copilot experience.

Background

- The Multi-Chat feature (previously called Sub-Sessions) is currently available for the Copilot harness and works in AHP sessions for Copilot.
- Team feedback and user studies have shown confusion around the feature and its name; the UX should be consistent across harnesses rather than Copilot-only.
- Claude AHP sessions do not currently show the Multi-Chat UI.

Proposal

- Implement Multi-Chat in the Claude harness with parity to the Copilot implementation and UX.
- Ensure Multi-Chat is available in AHP sessions for Claude as it is for Copilot.
- Minimize agent integration effort (sessions should be transparent to agents where possible), and document any agent-facing changes required.
- Update tests, e2e scenarios, and relevant documentation to reflect Multi-Chat availability in the Claude harness.

Acceptance criteria

- Multi-Chat UI appears and behaves the same in the Claude harness as it does in Copilot.
- Multi-Chat is available and functional in AHP sessions for Claude.
- Agent/handler code for Claude either requires no changes or any required changes are documented and minimal.
- Relevant tests and documentation updated.

Implementation notes

- Verify whether sessions need to be linked or if the agent surface can remain unchanged (transparent sessions).
- Coordinate UX changes with the Copilot harness team to ensure consistency and avoid repeating prior confusion around naming/behavior.
- Add testing steps to validate in manual and automated tests across the Claude harness and AHP sessions.

---

Split from the combined Claude & Codex issue. Codex tracked separately in 323624.

It would be highly beneficial to introduce an opt-in "Listen to PRs" background feature that monitors active Pull Requests for incoming review comments and integrates directly with Copilot Chat to streamline the feedback loop.

Currently, context switching between PR review platforms and the IDE to address comments is a manual and disruptive process. This feature would automatically capture PR feedback and present actionable, AI-driven resolution paths directly within VS Code.

Proposed Implementation:

 Smart Notification System: Upon receiving PR comments, VS Code triggers a toast notification. This system should include a configurable debounce/delay (e.g., 2-3 minutes) to batch multiple comments into a single notification and account for immediate reviewer retractions.
 Triage Actions: The consolidated notification should offer three primary resolution paths:
 1. Review Manually: Opens the standard PR diff view for human intervention.
 2. Suggest with Copilot: Opens a new Copilot Chat session, automatically attaching the relevant file context and pre-filling a prompt based on the reviewer's feedback. The user can then review, edit, and send the prompt.
 3. Auto (Agentic Mode): Delegates the resolution to Copilot, allowing it to autonomously perform code changes to address the feedback or draft direct replies to the PR comments.
 Context Menu Enhancement: Extend the existing + (Add Context) menu in the Copilot Chat UI to explicitly include "PR Comments" as a selectable data source, enabling users to easily bind review feedback to standard chat queries.

This workflow significantly reduces the friction of the code review process, allowing developers to leverage AI to resolve PR feedback seamlessly and efficiently.

Context

323037 (Phases 18–19) adds native / BYOK access for the Claude agent host: when claudeUseCopilotProxy: false host config is set, the Claude Agent SDK talks to whatever claude is configured to directly on the user's own credentials instead of routing through the Copilot proxy.

Today this is a hidden, host-level config flag (agent-host-config.json) with no UI affordance and no guidance when auth fails. This issue tracks making the feature discoverable and the proxy-vs-native choice legible to users.

 Ideas

- [ ] Auto-disable the proxy when the user isn't authenticated to GitHub. If there's no Copilot/GitHub auth, defaulting to (or falling back to) native BYO removes a dead end where proxy mode can never work.
- [ ] Surface the native vs. Copilot choice when picking a model for the first time. Make the transport an explicit, one-time choice in the model picker rather than a buried config flag.
- [ ] Show "configure Claude BYOK" docs on an auth error. When a native turn fails with an auth error, surface actionable guidance with a link to docs for setting up your own Anthropic credentials.
- [ ] Add a VS Code setting that forwards to the host setting. A workbench-level setting (e.g. chat.agentHost.claude.useCopilotProxy) that pushes down to the agent host's claudeUseCopilotProxy root config, so users don't have to hand-edit agent-host-config.json.

Feature request

When a tree item is revealed — either programmatically via the extension TreeView.reveal() API, or by built-in auto-reveal in the Explorer / Source Control views — the item is scrolled to the top edge of the viewport, with no surrounding rows visible. You lose all sense of where the item sits among its siblings (the files immediately above/below it).

The underlying list/tree widget already supports revealing an element at a fractional vertical position internally (the tree's reveal(element, relativeTop) / list reveal plumbing). That capability just isn't surfaced anywhere a consumer can reach it:

1. Extension API gap — TreeView.reveal(element, { select, focus, expand }) has no option to control scroll alignment. An extension that reveals a node cannot ask for it to be centered or shown with surrounding context; it always lands pinned to the top.
2. No user setting — Explorer / SCM auto-reveal always pins the revealed item to the top edge. explorer.autoReveal is only true | false | "focusNoScroll", and focusNoScroll suppresses scrolling, which is the opposite of wanting context.

 Proposal

1. Add an optional alignment to the TreeView.reveal options, e.g. reveal(element, { select, focus, expand, alignment?: 'top' | 'center' }) (or a numeric relativeTop), surfacing the existing internal capability to extensions.
2. Optionally, a user setting for built-in auto-reveal alignment, e.g. explorer.revealAlignment / scm.revealAlignment: "top" | "center".

 Why this isn't a duplicate

Earlier discussions (63406, and related 23902 / 65549) led to removing always-centered reveal in favour of top-pinning. This request isn't asking to flip the default back — it asks to make alignment configurable / API-exposed so both preferences are served, rather than hard-coding one. kept_issues.body:
## Feature request

When a tree item is revealed — either programmatically via the extension `TreeView.reveal()` API, or by built-in auto-reveal in the Explorer / Source Control views — the item is scrolled to the **top edge** of the viewport, with no surrounding rows visible. You lose all sense of *where* the item sits among its siblings (the files immediately above/below it).

The underlying list/tree widget already supports revealing an element at a **fractional vertical position** internally (the tree's `reveal(element, relativeTop)` / list `reveal` plumbing). That capability just isn't surfaced anywhere a consumer can reach it:

1. **Extension API gap** — `TreeView.reveal(element, { select, focus, expand })` has no option to control scroll alignment. An extension that reveals a node cannot ask for it to be centered or shown with surrounding context; it always lands pinned to the top.
2. **No user setting** — Explorer / SCM auto-reveal always pins the revealed item to the top edge. `explorer.autoReveal` is only `true | false | "focusNoScroll"`, and `focusNoScroll` *suppresses* scrolling, which is the opposite of wanting context.

## Proposal

1. Add an optional alignment to the `TreeView.reveal` options, e.g. `reveal(element, { select, focus, expand, alignment?: 'top' | 'center' })` (or a numeric `relativeTop`), surfacing the existing internal capability to extensions.
2. Optionally, a user setting for built-in auto-reveal alignment, e.g. `explorer.revealAlignment` / `scm.revealAlignment`: `"top" | "center"`.

## Why this isn't a duplicate

Earlier discussions (#63406, and related #23902 / #65549) led to *removing* always-centered reveal in favour of top-pinning. This request isn't asking to flip the default back — it asks to make alignment **configurable / API-exposed** so both preferences are served, rather than hard-coding one. The "reveal with context" behaviour matters for review workflows where an extension steps through items and reveals each one.

## Use case

I maintain a git-diff-review extension that reveals the file currently under review in the SCM/Explorer tree as the user steps through changes. Because reveal pins to the top edge, the reviewed file ends up flush against the top with no visible context. An alignment option (or a `relativeTop`) would let the extension reveal it with a few rows of breathing room above and below.
kept_issues.title: Expose reveal scroll-alignment to the TreeView API (and an Explorer/SCM "reveal with context" option)

Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Extensions can create integrated terminals with vscode.window.createTerminal, and can choose locations such as the panel, editor area, or a split beside a parent terminal via location: { parentTerminal }.

However, there does not appear to be a public API for creating a new terminal adjacent to a related existing terminal while keeping the terminal UI as a flat tab list.

For example, an extension command may create a new terminal using the current working directory of the active terminal. If the active terminal is named infra, the new terminal is logically related to infra, so it would be useful for the new terminal to appear immediately after infra in the terminal tab list.

Currently the extension can either:

- create a normal terminal with the desired cwd, but VS Code decides the tab order
- create a split terminal with location: { parentTerminal }, but that changes the UI layout into a split pane

Neither option preserves a flat terminal tab list while keeping related terminals grouped together.

 Related issues

I found these related issues before filing this:

- 253020 requested broader terminal tab reordering APIs and was closed as out of scope.
- 309068 requested move terminal tab up/down commands and was closed after not reaching the upvote threshold.

This request is intentionally narrower than a general-purpose terminal reordering API. It focuses on creation-time placement for a newly created terminal, specifically adjacent to a parent/source terminal.

 Describe the solution you'd like

Add a way for extensions to create a terminal next to an existing terminal without creating a split pane.

One possible API shape:

 

Another possible API shape could extend terminal location options:

 

The exact API shape is not important; the important part is allowing extensions to keep a new terminal adjacent to a related terminal without forcing a split layout.

 Describe alternatives you've considered

- location: { parentTerminal }: creates a split, which is useful for some workflows but not for users who want a flat terminal tab list.
- Creating the terminal normally and naming it after the source terminal: helps identify related terminals, but does not keep them grouped in the UI.
- Manual drag-and-drop after creation: works interactively, but cannot support an extension command that consistently preserves workflow grouping.

 Additional context

This would help extensions that create workflow-specific terminals from an existing terminal context, such as:

- creating another terminal in the active terminal's current working directory
- opening task-specific terminals next to their source terminal
- grouping terminals by project or service without changing the terminal panel layout into splits

The goal is not full terminal layout management, only a small creation-time placement hint for related terminals.

Extensions can create integrated terminals with `vscode.window.createTerminal`, and can choose locations such as the panel, editor area, or a split beside a parent terminal via `location: { parentTerminal }`.

However, there does not appear to be a public API for creating a new terminal adjacent to a related existing terminal while keeping the terminal UI as a flat tab list.

For example, an extension command may create a new terminal using the current working directory of the active terminal. If the active terminal is named `infra`, the new terminal is logically related to `infra`, so it would be useful for the new terminal to appear immediately after `infra` in the terminal tab list.

Currently the extension can either:

- create a normal terminal with the desired `cwd`, but VS Code decides the tab order
- create a split terminal with `location: { parentTerminal }`, but that changes the UI layout into a split pane

Neither option preserves a flat terminal tab list while keeping related terminals grouped together.

- #253020 requested broader terminal tab reordering APIs and was closed as out of scope.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a way for extensions to create a terminal next to an existing terminal without creating a split pane.

One possible API shape:

```ts
const terminal = vscode.window.createTerminal({
  cwd,
  location: vscode.TerminalLocation.Panel,
  insertAfter: parentTerminal,
});
```

Another possible API shape could extend terminal location options:

```ts
const terminal = vscode.window.createTerminal({
  cwd,
  location: {
    parentTerminal,
    split: false,
    placement: "after",
  },
});
```

The exact API shape is not important; the important part is allowing extensions to keep a new terminal adjacent to a related terminal without forcing a split layout.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Manual drag-and-drop after creation: works interactively, but cannot support an extension command that consistently preserves workflow grouping.

This would help extensions that create workflow-specific terminals from an existing terminal context, such as:

- creating another terminal in the active terminal's current working directory
- opening task-specific terminals next to their source terminal
- grouping terminals by project or service without changing the terminal panel layout into splits

The goal is not full terminal layout management, only a small creation-time placement hint for related terminals.

Problem

Extension webviews currently can't use navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia at all — the webview iframe carries no allow="camera; microphone", and the Electron permission handler denies media for vscode-webview:// origins. That's intentional ("media must not be silently accessible", 113916), but it leaves no opt-in path for legitimate, user-initiated scenarios: live device/camera preview, audio/video capture, QR scanning, in-editor calls, voice/accessibility input, hardware diagnostics.

Today the only workaround is to spawn ffmpeg in the extension host and stream frames back into the webview — heavy and platform-specific, just to reach hardware the OS already exposes.

 Precedent

There's now an active precedent: consent-gated, per-origin, revocable camera/mic/location permissions for the integrated browser (299521 / PR 322639), currently in Insiders. This proposes extending that same safety model to extension webviews.

 Proposed shape (designed to answer the "no silent access" concern)

- Extension opts in via a proposed API (webviewMediaDevices) and declares devices on the webview — mediaDevices: ['camera', 'microphone'] — visible at install time, off by default.
- The iframe allow is injected only for declaring webviews (per-device).
- First getUserMedia triggers a one-time consent prompt; the grant is stored per extension and is revocable.
- No declaration → no allow; no consent → no access.

 Working PoC (desktop), behind the proposed API

Verified end-to-end (declare → consent prompt → getUserMedia → live camera/mic in the webview). Deliberately minimal; happy to rework to your conventions, not asking to merge as-is:
 

The net-new piece vs the browser work is mainly the iframe allow injection (on both the outer webview iframe and the inner content frame, for Permissions-Policy delegation) plus the per-extension grant; the consent UI/store could be reused.

 The ask

Would the team be open to this direction? If so, we'll productionize (persisted/revocable grants + management UI, renderer-brokered consent, remote/web/WSL hosts).

 Related
- 250568 — Permissions-policy violation report (microphone not allowed in a webview)
- 113916 — earlier decision that webview media should be blocked without a prompt
- 299521 / PR 322639 — consent-gated browser permissions (in Insiders), the model this builds on

### Problem

Extension webviews currently can't use `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` at all — the webview iframe carries no `allow="camera; microphone"`, and the Electron permission handler denies `media` for `vscode-webview://` origins. That's intentional ("media must not be silently accessible", #113916), but it leaves **no opt-in path** for legitimate, user-initiated scenarios: live device/camera preview, audio/video capture, QR scanning, in-editor calls, voice/accessibility input, hardware diagnostics.

Today the only workaround is to spawn `ffmpeg` in the extension host and stream frames back into the webview — heavy and platform-specific, just to reach hardware the OS already exposes.

### Precedent

There's now an active precedent: consent-gated, per-origin, revocable camera/mic/location permissions for the integrated browser (#299521 / PR #322639), **currently in Insiders**. This proposes extending that same safety model to extension webviews.

### Proposed shape (designed to answer the "no silent access" concern)

- Extension opts in via a proposed API (`webviewMediaDevices`) and declares devices on the webview — `mediaDevices: ['camera', 'microphone']` — visible at install time, off by default.
- The iframe `allow` is injected **only** for declaring webviews (per-device).
- First `getUserMedia` triggers a **one-time consent prompt**; the grant is stored **per extension** and is revocable.
- No declaration → no `allow`; no consent → no access.

### Working PoC (desktop), behind the proposed API

Verified end-to-end (declare → consent prompt → `getUserMedia` → live camera/mic in the webview). Deliberately minimal; happy to rework to your conventions, not asking to merge as-is:
https://github.com/chrisdp/vscode/commit/5b9064c626cbc87554c65f0639fa9062d86b72e6

The net-new piece vs the browser work is mainly the iframe `allow` injection (on both the outer webview iframe and the inner content frame, for Permissions-Policy delegation) plus the per-extension grant; the consent UI/store could be reused.

### The ask

Would the team be open to this direction? If so, we'll productionize (persisted/revocable grants + management UI, renderer-brokered consent, remote/web/WSL hosts).

### Related
- #250568 — Permissions-policy violation report (microphone not allowed in a webview)
- #113916 — earlier decision that webview media should be blocked without a prompt
- #299521 / PR #322639 — consent-gated browser permissions (in Insiders), the model this builds on

I’d like to propose a feature for the integrated browser that lets a repo or page provide custom context when a user selects an element and chooses “Add Element to Chat”.

In short, it would enable react-grab like functionality through a hook with the code defined in repo. There are a lot of "grab" libraries designed for different web frameworks: react, angular, svelte, solidjs, vue, etc... This feature would enable these tools to work inside the integrated browser directly. Each framework would have its own npm package to enable the hook on the browser side.

Today, the flow in browserEditorChatFeatures.ts builds a standardized snippet from the selected DOM element (HTML, path, dimensions, computed styles, etc.) and sends that into chat. That is useful, but it is not flexible enough for repos with specialized needs.

As a frontend developer, I want to be able to customize the text snippet that gets attached to chat so I can provide richer, repo-specific context to agents. This should make agent-driven edits more accurate and reduce the need for manual follow-up.

Example use case:
- In a React repo, I want the browser selection flow to call custom code that inspects the React virtual DOM / component tree and returns a structured component-context summary.
- I also want to customize CSS output, for example to de-transform CSS module class names before they are attached to chat, or to remove hashed griffel class names.

Proposal:
- When an element is selected in the integrated browser, VS Code should attempt to invoke a page-provided hook that can customize the context payload.
- The hook should be available for both:
 - the manual “Add Element to Chat” flow from the integrated browser UI, and
 - the browser-tool / agent-driven selection path, so the same repo-specific context can be provided regardless of how the selection was triggered.
- The hook could be exposed as an optional global function on the page, for example:
 - window.__vscodeIntegratedBrowserGetContext?.(elementData)
- The hook should be able to return either:
 - a string snippet to append to the existing context, or
 - a richer structured payload that VS Code can render into the chat attachment.
- If the hook is not provided, the current built-in behavior remains unchanged.
- For discoverability, we could add a small docs/help entry or info popover near the element-selection button in the integrated browser UI.

Why this is valuable:
- Different repos need different context
- Frontend teams often want framework-specific summaries
- Better context should lead to better agent suggestions and edits

Possible follow-up work:
- Support repo-specific injection via a script already loaded in the page
- Provide a documented API shape and examples
- Add a UI hint/docs link near the selection action
- Add some default formatters for common libraries like react

---

You can contact me directly on Teams at my Microsoft alias

Problem
When using comprehensive keyboard layout extensions or modal editing wrappers like Master Key, the keybindings.json file size can drastically increase due to the sheer volume of generated shortcuts for various modes and contexts. 

Currently, VS Code strictly enforces a 100kb limit on the keyboard shortcuts file for Settings Sync, throwing the following error and disabling keyboard settings synchronization:
> Disabled syncing keyboard shortcuts because size of the keyboard shortcuts file to sync is larger than 100kb. Please open the file and reduce the size and enable sync

This hard limit penalizes power users who rely on heavy keybinding configurations or ecosystem-altering extensions.

 Describe the solution you'd like
I would like VS Code to increase the maximum allowed file size for keybindings.json in Settings Sync from 100kb to 200kb (or higher). This slight overhead would easily accommodate complex, extension-generated keybinding maps without risking server performance.

 Describe alternatives you've considered
 Manually stripping keybindings: Not viable as it breaks the functionality provided by key-mapping extensions.
 Disabling keybindings sync: A frustrating workaround since keyboard shortcuts are a core part of an engineer's workflow synchronization across multiple machines.

 Additional context
86178

﻿ Feature Request: Three enhancements for BYOK (chatLanguageModels.json) configuration experience

 Suggestion 1: Auto-detect and auto-encrypt plaintext apiKey on file save / Provide a command to bulk-set encrypted apiKey

Problem:

When users manually edit chatLanguageModels.json to configure custom providers, they may write the apiKey in plaintext (e.g., when migrating from third-party tools or batch-importing many providers). Currently, VS Code's BYOK system only encrypts apiKey via SecretStorageService when provider groups are created through the UI wizard or programmatic API — the _resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup method handles this, but it is never triggered on file save.

For users managing many custom endpoints, manually clicking through the UI for each API key is impractical.

Desired improvement — auto-encrypt on file save (plaintext in file → auto encrypted):

 

After saving, the system should automatically:
1. Detect plaintext apiKey values in provider group configurations.
2. Migrate them to SecretStorageService (as it already does in _resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup).
3. Rewrite the file with encrypted placeholder references (e.g., "${input:chat.lm.secret. }").

Additionally, exposing a command (e.g., workbench.action.providers.setApiKey) accessible via Ctrl+P would allow external tooling and batch scripts to programmatically set encrypted API keys.

Relevant code:
- _resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup in src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts
- LanguageModelsConfigurationService in src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/languageModelsConfigurationService.ts — file watcher exists but no auto-encryption.
- updateLanguageModelsProviderGroupApiKey — existing UI-only command.

---

﻿## Feature Request: Three enhancements for BYOK (`chatLanguageModels.json`) configuration experience

### Suggestion 1: Auto-detect and auto-encrypt plaintext `apiKey` on file save / Provide a command to bulk-set encrypted `apiKey`

**Problem:**

When users manually edit `chatLanguageModels.json` to configure custom providers, they may write the `apiKey` in plaintext (e.g., when migrating from third-party tools or batch-importing many providers). Currently, VS Code's BYOK system only encrypts `apiKey` via `SecretStorageService` when provider groups are created through the **UI wizard or programmatic API** — the `_resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup` method handles this, but it is never triggered on file save.

For users managing many custom endpoints, manually clicking through the UI for each API key is impractical.

**Desired improvement — auto-encrypt on file save (plaintext in file → auto encrypted):**

```json
[
    {
        "name": "deepseek",
        "vendor": "customendpoint",
        // User writes plaintext apiKey manually in JSON file
        "apiKey": "sk-01234...abcdef",
        "apiType": "messages"
    }
]
```

After saving, the system should automatically:
1. Detect plaintext `apiKey` values in provider group configurations.
2. Migrate them to `SecretStorageService` (as it already does in `_resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup`).
3. Rewrite the file with encrypted placeholder references (e.g., `"${input:chat.lm.secret.<hash>}"`).

Additionally, exposing a **command** (e.g., `workbench.action.providers.setApiKey`) accessible via `Ctrl+P` would allow external tooling and batch scripts to programmatically set encrypted API keys.

**Relevant code:**
- `_resolveLanguageModelProviderGroup` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts`
- `LanguageModelsConfigurationService` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/languageModelsConfigurationService.ts` — file watcher exists but no auto-encryption.
- `updateLanguageModelsProviderGroupApiKey` — existing UI-only command.

---

### Suggestion 2: Add `apiUrl` and `defaults` at the provider group level to avoid per-model duplication

**Problem:**

When multiple models share the same base endpoint and capabilities under one provider group, each model must still repeat `url`, `maxInputTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `toolCalling`, `vision`, etc. This creates excessive boilerplate:

```json
[
    {
        "name": "deepseek",
        "vendor": "customendpoint",
        "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.-f1cf4fa}",
        "apiType": "messages",
        "models": [
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-flash",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-flash",
                "url": "https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic",
                "toolCalling": true,
                "vision": false,
                "maxInputTokens": 128000,
                "maxOutputTokens": 128000
            },
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                "url": "https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic",
                "toolCalling": true,
                "vision": false,
                "maxInputTokens": 128000,
                "maxOutputTokens": 128000
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

**Desired improvement — inherited defaults at group level:**

```json
[
    {
        "name": "deepseek",
        "vendor": "customendpoint",
        "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.-f1cf4fa}",
        "apiType": "messages",
        // Base URL for all models in this group
        "apiUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic",
        // Default capability params — models inherit unless overridden
        "defaults": {
            "toolCalling": true,
            "vision": false,
            "maxInputTokens": 128000,
            "maxOutputTokens": 128000
        },
        "models": [
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-flash",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-flash"
            },
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                // Per-model overrides when defaults don't apply
                "maxInputTokens": 256000,
                "maxOutputTokens": 256000
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

The resolution order should be: **per-model field > `defaults` at group level > provider-level fallback**. This would dramatically reduce boilerplate and make bulk editing much easier, especially for self-hosted endpoints with many models.

**Relevant code:**
- `CustomEndpointModelProviderConfig` / `_CustomOAIModelConfig` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/byok/vscode-node/customEndpointProvider.ts` and `customOAIProvider.ts` — per-model `url` is currently required for each entry.
- `getAllModels` in those same files — builds per-model info from `configuration.models`.

---

### Suggestion 3: Add `apiListModels` endpoint to auto-discover and sync available models

**Problem:**

Currently, when a user configures a new provider (especially a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint), they must manually enumerate every model ID in the `models` array. For endpoints that support model listing (e.g., `GET /v1/models`), this is redundant. The user has to keep the list in sync manually whenever the upstream adds or removes models.

**Desired improvement — auto-fetch from model list endpoint:**

```json
[
    {
        "name": "deepseek",
        "vendor": "customendpoint",
        "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.-f1cf4fa}",
        "apiType": "messages",
        "apiUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic",
        // Optional: auto-fetch available models from this discovery endpoint
        "apiListModels": "/v1/models",
        "defaults": {
            "toolCalling": true,
            "vision": false,
            "maxInputTokens": 128000,
            "maxOutputTokens": 128000
        },
        "models": [
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-flash",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-flash",
                // Not listed as hidden → visible in model picker
                "hidden": false
            },
            {
                "id": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                "name": "deepseek-v4-pro",
                "hidden": false
            },
            {
                "id": "deepseek-reasoner",
                "name": "DeepSeek Reasoner",
                // Hide this model from the picker by default
                "hidden": true
            }
        ]
    }
]
```

When `apiListModels` is specified, the system would:
1. Fetch available models from the endpoint (similar to how `AbstractOpenAICompatibleLMProvider.getModelsFromEndpoint` works).
2. Merge the server-side model list with the user's local `models` array.
3. Use the user-configured `hidden` property (or a new `show`/`hide` toggle in the model picker UI) to control visibility, rather than requiring the user to maintain a complete list.

This approach — **maintain model list automatically, let the user just toggle show/hide** — would be far more efficient and user-friendly for self-hosted providers that frequently add or update models.

**Relevant code:**
- `AbstractOpenAICompatibleLMProvider.getModelsFromEndpoint` in `extensions/copilot/src/extension/byok/vscode-node/abstractLanguageModelChatProvider.ts` — already fetches models from a discovery URL; could be extended to support user-provided `apiListModels`.
- `LanguageModelsService.setModelHidden` / `setGroupHidden` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts` — existing show/hide infrastructure for models.
- `getAllModels` in `customEndpointProvider.ts` — when `configuration.url` is set, falls back to `super.getAllModels()` which fetches from endpoint; this pattern could be extended.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

 VS Code Version: 1.126
 OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise (26200) — corporate managed

 Steps to Reproduce

1. In a project workspace that handles customer/regulated data, open .vscode/settings.json.
2. Add "telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off".
3. Observe the setting is ignored — value only takes effect when placed in User (application) settings.

 The problem

telemetry.telemetryLevel is registered with ConfigurationScope.APPLICATION and restricted: true (see src/vs/platform/telemetry/common/telemetryService.ts). This means:

- A developer working on multiple projects on a corporate-managed machine cannot say "telemetry off for this workspace (which contains customer data under NDA) but leave the org-wide policy value in place for other projects."
- The only escape hatches today are the org-wide GPO/enterprise policy (TelemetryLevel), or flipping the user setting each time you switch projects — both are heavy hammers.

Peer editors solve this: JetBrains IDEs allow project-level opt-out of Data Sharing that stacks over the application default. VS Code's own http.proxy, git.enabled, and other sensitive settings support workspace scope with the restricted flag gating trusted-workspace behaviour — so there is precedent for this pattern.

 Proposal

Either:

(a) Widen the scope of telemetry.telemetryLevel to ConfigurationScope.WINDOW (or RESOURCE), keeping restricted: true so only trusted workspaces can lower the level. The value would monotonically decrease telemetry (workspace can only set ≤ application level) — never raise it above what the user/policy allows.

(b) Add a new sibling setting e.g. telemetry.workspaceOverride (enum: inherit | off, default inherit, scope WINDOW, restricted: true). off clamps the effective level to off for the window; anything else inherits the app-level value.

Option (a) is cleaner if the monotonic-decrease guarantee is acceptable. Option (b) is safer if you want to keep the primary setting application-scoped and add opt-in workspace clamp.

 Why this matters for corp/enterprise use

Enterprise VS Code users with mixed public/regulated projects on the same laptop currently either:
- Accept org-wide telemetry level for all workspaces (may leak metadata about regulated project structure).
- Manually toggle the user setting each context switch (error-prone).

A workspace-scoped clamp gives per-project rigor without disturbing the org-wide baseline.

 Not a duplicate of

Searched for telemetry workspace scope, telemetry.telemetryLevel workspace, telemetry per workspace project — no existing issue captures this ask. 260375 covers tool enablement, not telemetry scope. If I missed one, happy to close.

Feature request

In Quick Open (Go to File), you can type a file path followed by : or : : to open a file at a specific position. It would be useful to also support a line range using a hyphen, so that pressing Enter opens the file with that range selected.

 Proposed syntax

- file.txt:20-40 → select from the start of line 20 to the start of line 40
- file.txt:20:3-40:5 → select from line 20, col 3 to line 40, col 5
- file.txt:20:3-40 → end column defaults to the start of the end line
- Should also work with the existing separator/style variants: file.txt203-40,5, file.txt(20,3-40,5)

This mirrors the range syntax VS Code already uses for markdown document links (L10-L20), so a bare 10-20 selects from the start of line 10 to the start of line 20.

 Notes

- The parsing lives in extractRangeFromFilter (src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/common/search.ts), which is reached through the file picker (AnythingQuickAccessProvider).

Addressed by 324318.

The number of chat sessions retained in the history panel is hard-coded to 50 in chatSessionStore.ts:

50 is far too low for anyone who uses Copilot Chat heavily. Sessions fall off the list within days.

 Proposed Solution

Expose maxPersistedSessions as a VS Code setting, for example:

kept_issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->


## Problem

The number of chat sessions retained in the history panel is hard-coded to 50 in `chatSessionStore.ts`:

```typescript
// src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatSessionStore.ts
const maxPersistedSessions = 50;
```

`trimEntries()` runs on every shutdown and permanently deletes index entries beyond that limit (sorted by `lastMessageDate`). There is no way for a user to recover deleted sessions — even if the underlying JSONL files still exist on disk — because the index entry is gone.

50 is far too low for anyone who uses Copilot Chat heavily. Sessions fall off the list within days.

## Proposed Solution

Expose `maxPersistedSessions` as a VS Code setting, for example:

```json
"chat.session.maxPersistedSessions": {
  "type": "number",
  "default": 50,
  "minimum": 10,
  "markdownDescription": "Maximum number of chat sessions to retain in history. Sessions beyond this limit are removed oldest-first when VS Code closes. Set to a higher value if you frequently lose access to older sessions."
}
```

`trimEntries()` would read from the settings service instead of the hard-coded constant, keeping the default behaviour unchanged.

## Workaround

Users currently have to patch `workbench.desktop.main.js` directly to raise the limit, which is wiped on every VS Code update.
kept_issues.title: chat: make maximum persisted sessions a user-configurable setting

- Entry point: window.registerTerminalProfileProvider(id, { provideTerminalProfile(token) }) — the callback only receives a CancellationToken, never the cwd.
- Where the info exists but is dropped: VS Code's multi-root picker result flows internally as ICreateContributedTerminalProfileOptions.cwd into extHostTerminalService.$createContributedProfileTerminal(id, options). Proposal
- Let user manually handle collapsibleState of vscode.TreeItems, similar to checkboxState.
- Add additional option to vscode.window.createTreeView, like manageCollapsibleStateManually.
 - User must subscribe to onDidExpandElement and onDidCollapseElement to received changes.
- The collapsibleState of the vscode.TreeItem is used (provided by the vscode.TreeDataProvider.getElement method) just like the first time an item is drawn.

 Why
I need to programatically change the collapsible state of my tree items. Sometimes, I want them to collapse and sometimes I want them to expand. 

 Related issues
My feature request is similar to 55879, which led to the implementation of vscode.TreeView.reveal(element, options). However, reveal doesn't solve the actual problem and brings other problems. 
1. 92176 The collapsible counter part (something like hide), is still missing and in backlog.
2. Reveal also keeps the revealed item in the view. In my case, I just need to expand the parent. I do not care and do not want the view to scroll to the item reveal. I don't want the view to scroll at all. This is related to 323192, where a scroll alignment is proposed. 
3. 286332 This is a problem I also already encountered. Would be solved by the proposal. vscode.TreeView.onDidExpandElement would fire and user could decide to elapsed element but he could also keep the item collapsed and do nothing.

 Questions I couldn't directly answer
- What exactly is shown by the view after items are collapsed/expanded?
 - Main idea is to keep the view as is and do not scroll up or down
 - What happens when we basically collapse all? The view has to scroll up to the parent items still shown
 - What happens when we expand all? What does "do not scroll" mean in this context? 
 - => What exactly is the anker the view should return on a redraw?
- It would make sense to have onDidExpandElement/onDidCollapseElement only get invoked if the user directly, or indirectly changes the collapsible state OR, vscode.TreeView.reveal is called. Though, reveal looses a bit of purpose, if one doesn't need to select, focus, or expand an element.
- Maybe it would make more sense, to fuse onDidExpandElement and onDidCollapseElement, similar to onDidChangeCheckboxState event. The Event would then contain the (potential) new collapseState. 

 Workaround how this already kinda works
We can already refresh the tree view with an empty array, thus drawing nothing. Then we draw the same view, just with updated collapsible states. However, this takes time and is ugly.

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

# Proposal
- Let user manually handle `collapsibleState` of `vscode.TreeItems`, similar to `checkboxState`.
- Add additional option to `vscode.window.createTreeView`, like `manageCollapsibleStateManually`.
  - User must subscribe to `onDidExpandElement` and `onDidCollapseElement` to received changes.
- The `collapsibleState` of the `vscode.TreeItem` is used (provided by the `vscode.TreeDataProvider.getElement` method) just like the first time an item is drawn.

# Why
I need to programatically change the collapsible state of my tree items. Sometimes, I want them to collapse and sometimes I want them to expand. 

# Related issues
My feature request is similar to #55879, which led to the implementation of `vscode.TreeView.reveal(element, options)`. However, `reveal` doesn't solve the actual problem and brings other problems. 
1. #92176 The collapsible counter part (something like hide), is still missing and in backlog.
2. Reveal also keeps the revealed item in the view. In my case, I just need to expand the parent. I do not care and do not want the view to scroll to the item reveal. I don't want the view to scroll at all. This is related to #323192, where a scroll alignment is proposed. 
3. #286332 This is a problem I also already encountered. Would be solved by the proposal. `vscode.TreeView.onDidExpandElement` would fire and user could decide to elapsed element but he could also keep the item collapsed and do nothing.

# Questions I couldn't directly answer
- What exactly is shown by the view after items are collapsed/expanded?
  - Main idea is to keep the view as is and do not scroll up or down
  - What happens when we basically collapse all? The view has to scroll up to the parent items still shown
  - What happens when we expand all? What does "do not scroll" mean in this context? 
  - => What exactly is the anker the view should return on a redraw?
- It would make sense to have `onDidExpandElement`/`onDidCollapseElement` only get invoked if the user directly, or indirectly changes the collapsible state *OR*, `vscode.TreeView.reveal` is called. Though, `reveal` looses a bit of purpose, if one doesn't need to select, focus, or expand an element.
- Maybe it would make more sense, to fuse `onDidExpandElement` and `onDidCollapseElement`, similar to `onDidChangeCheckboxState` event. The Event would then contain the (potential) new `collapseState`. 

# Workaround how this already kinda works
We can already refresh the tree view with an empty array, thus drawing nothing. Then we draw the same view, just with updated collapsible states. However, this takes time and is ugly.
kept_issues.title: Add option for manual handling of collapsibleState similar to manageCheckboxStateManually

Problem

When an extension registers a custom editor with default priority for a file type, that editor also hijacks the diff and merge views for that file type. This happens purely from the contribution — no workbench.editorAssociations entry is needed — because diff/merge inherit the textEditor priority. So an extension has no way to provide a great normal editor for a file type without also taking over its diffs and merges.

The same applies when a user opts a custom editor in via settings. For example:

 

...makes .md diffs open the Markdown editor side-by-side instead of the normal text diff editor. The only escape hatch is an opt-out per extension: users have to add a second setting to reset diffs back to the default:

 

This is the wrong default. Every custom editor that provides a normal editor would require users to reset the diff association. It should be opt-in: a custom editor should be used for diffs/merges only if it explicitly says so.

 Proposal

Introduce a never editor priority and make diff/merge opt-in for custom editors.

1. New never priority

Add RegisteredEditorPriority.never (and CustomEditorPriority.never). Priorities are resolved per input type — normal editor, diff editor, and merge editor — and never for a given input type means:

- The editor is never auto-selected for that input type (normal, diff, or merge).
- It is skipped for that input type even when a general workbench.editorAssociations entry points at it.
- It can still be reached explicitly via Reopen Editor With…, or forced by the specialized workbench.diffEditorAssociations / merge association.

2. Diff/merge opt out by default for custom editors

Resolve the customEditors contribution point priority per input type:

- priority: "default" (or any string) expands to { textEditor: , diff: never, merge: never }.
- Omitting priority yields { textEditor: option, diff: never, merge: never }.
- diffEditor / mergeEditor no longer inherit from textEditor; they default to never and must be set explicitly (behind the customEditorPriority API proposal) for the editor to participate in diffs/merges.

3. Resolution respects never

The "which user association may select an editor" step filters out general editorAssociations entries whose editor is never for the requested input type. The specialized diffEditorAssociations setting is still allowed to force a never editor, since choosing it is an explicit, diff-scoped decision.

 Behavior summary

| Setting | Normal editor | Diff / merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| editorAssociations: .md → vscode.markdown.editor | Markdown editor | Text diff editor (was: Markdown side-by-side) — vscode.markdown.editor has diffEditor: never |
| editorAssociations: .md → vscode.markdown.preview.editor | Markdown Preview | Markdown Preview — this editor opts in with diffEditor: option, so the association applies to diffs too |
| diffEditorAssociations: .md → vscode.markdown.editor | (unchanged) | Markdown editor (forced) |
| Custom editor declares priority.diffEditor: default | per textEditor | Custom editor participates in diffs |

 Compatibility

- Custom editors that only provide a normal editor no longer need users to reset diffEditorAssociations.
- Breaking for extensions relying on implicit diff registration: an extension that registers a default editor is currently used for diffs automatically. With the priority mechanism, diff/merge default to never, so such extensions must now explicitly opt in via priority.diffEditor / priority.mergeEditor to keep participating in diffs/merges. A registration-time warning can flag editors that provide a diff factory without opting in.
- Existing resolver-level string priorities (used by built-in registrations via toRegisteredEditorPriorityInfo) still expand to all-equal priorities, so built-in diff behavior is unaffected.

---

Additionally, there is to make it easier to discover/switch to custom editors.

 Verification steps

1. Add to settings.json:
 
2. Open a .md file — it opens in the Markdown custom editor. ✅ (association still applies to the normal editor)
3. Open a diff of a .md file (e.g. from the SCM view or git.openChange) — it opens in the text diff editor, not the Markdown editor side-by-side. ✅ (custom editor opts out of diffs by default; no diffEditorAssociations reset needed)
4. Now add:
 
 Re-open the .md diff — it now uses the Markdown editor. ✅ (specialized diff association forces the never editor)
5. Remove the diff association again and use Reopen Editor With… on a .md diff — the Markdown editor is still offered and works when picked. ✅ (never only blocks automatic/association selection, not explicit choice)
6. Sanity check an exclusive custom editor (e.g. the Hex editor): its behavior is unchanged.
kept_issues.body:
### Problem

When an extension registers a custom editor with `default` priority for a file type, that editor also hijacks the **diff** and **merge** views for that file type. This happens purely from the contribution — no `workbench.editorAssociations` entry is needed — because diff/merge inherit the `textEditor` priority. So an extension has no way to provide a great normal editor for a file type without also taking over its diffs and merges.

The same applies when a user opts a custom editor in via settings. For example:

```jsonc
"workbench.editorAssociations": {
  "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
}
```

...makes `*.md` diffs open the Markdown editor side-by-side instead of the normal text diff editor. The only escape hatch is an **opt-out** per extension: users have to add a second setting to reset diffs back to the default:

```jsonc
"workbench.diffEditorAssociations": {
  "*.md": "default"
}
```

This is the wrong default. Every custom editor that provides a normal editor would require users to reset the diff association. It should be **opt-in**: a custom editor should be used for diffs/merges only if it explicitly says so.

### Proposal

Introduce a `never` editor priority and make diff/merge opt-in for custom editors.

**1. New `never` priority**

Add `RegisteredEditorPriority.never` (and `CustomEditorPriority.never`). Priorities are resolved per input type — normal editor, diff editor, and merge editor — and `never` for a given input type means:

- The editor is **never** auto-selected for that input type (normal, diff, or merge).
- It is **skipped** for that input type even when a general `workbench.editorAssociations` entry points at it.
- It can still be reached explicitly via `Reopen Editor With…`, or forced by the specialized `workbench.diffEditorAssociations` / merge association.

**2. Diff/merge opt out by default for custom editors**

Resolve the `customEditors` contribution point priority per input type:

- `priority: "default"` (or any string) expands to `{ textEditor: <value>, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- Omitting `priority` yields `{ textEditor: option, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- `diffEditor` / `mergeEditor` no longer inherit from `textEditor`; they default to `never` and must be set explicitly (behind the `customEditorPriority` API proposal) for the editor to participate in diffs/merges.

**3. Resolution respects `never`**

The "which user association may select an editor" step filters out general `editorAssociations` entries whose editor is `never` for the requested input type. The specialized `diffEditorAssociations` setting is still allowed to force a `never` editor, since choosing it is an explicit, diff-scoped decision.

### Behavior summary

| Setting | Normal editor | Diff / merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | Markdown editor | **Text diff editor** (was: Markdown side-by-side) — `vscode.markdown.editor` has `diffEditor: never` |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.preview.editor` | Markdown Preview | Markdown Preview — this editor opts in with `diffEditor: option`, so the association applies to diffs too |
| `diffEditorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | (unchanged) | Markdown editor (forced) |
| Custom editor declares `priority.diffEditor: default` | per `textEditor` | Custom editor participates in diffs |

### Compatibility

- Custom editors that only provide a normal editor no longer need users to reset `diffEditorAssociations`.
- **Breaking for extensions relying on implicit diff registration:** an extension that registers a default editor is currently used for diffs automatically. With the priority mechanism, diff/merge default to `never`, so such extensions must now **explicitly opt in** via `priority.diffEditor` / `priority.mergeEditor` to keep participating in diffs/merges. A registration-time warning can flag editors that provide a diff factory without opting in.
- Existing resolver-level string priorities (used by built-in registrations via `toRegisteredEditorPriorityInfo`) still expand to all-equal priorities, so built-in diff behavior is unaffected.

---

Additionally, there is https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324795 to make it easier to discover/switch to custom editors.

### Verification steps

1. Add to `settings.json`:
   ```jsonc
   "workbench.editorAssociations": {
     "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
   }
   ```
2. Open a `*.md` file — it opens in the Markdown custom editor. ✅ (association still applies to the normal editor)
3. Open a diff of a `*.md` file (e.g. from the SCM view or `git.openChange`) — it opens in the **text diff editor**, not the Markdown editor side-by-side. ✅ (custom editor opts out of diffs by default; no `diffEditorAssociations` reset needed)
4. Now add:
   ```jsonc
   "workbench.diffEditorAssociations": {
     "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
   }
   ```
   Re-open the `*.md` diff — it now uses the Markdown editor. ✅ (specialized diff association forces the `never` editor)
5. Remove the diff association again and use **Reopen Editor With…** on a `*.md` diff — the Markdown editor is still offered and works when picked. ✅ (`never` only blocks automatic/association selection, not explicit choice)
6. Sanity check an exclusive custom editor (e.g. the Hex editor): its behavior is unchanged.
kept_issues.title: Add never editor priority so custom editors opt out of diff/merge by default

kept_issues._normalized_body:
Problem

When a file can be opened by more than one editor (for example a .md file that can open in the text editor, the Markdown preview, or the Markdown editor), there is no obvious, always-visible way to see which editor is currently used or to switch to another one. Today users have to know about the Reopen Editor With… command, and there is no affordance in the editor chrome that surfaces the available editors.

This is especially relevant now that custom editors opt out of diffs/merges by default (324791): users may want to quickly switch a diff between the text diff editor and a custom diff editor, or set a per-extension default.

 Proposal

Add a small dropdown on the right-hand side of the breadcrumbs bar that shows the current editor type as text (for example "Markdown Preview", "Text Editor", or "Text Diff Editor" in a diff) and, when clicked, opens a menu to:

- Switch the active editor to any of the other editors that can open the resource (reuses reopenActiveEditorWith). The current editor is checked.
- Set Default for the file type via a submenu. In a diff context this writes to workbench.diffEditorAssociations; otherwise to workbench.editorAssociations. The currently configured default is checked.
- In a diff, Open Original / Open Modified as standalone editors.

Details:

- The dropdown only appears when a more specialized editor is available — i.e. more than one editor can open the resource. It is hidden for plain text files (only the default editor) and for exclusive editors such as the Hex editor (which return no alternatives).
- Extension-provided editors show their source (Label - Extension Name); built-in editors show just their label.
- In a diff context, the default text editor is labeled "Text Diff Editor" to match how it actually opens.
- Only shown on the dedicated breadcrumbs bar (tabbed mode), not the inline single-tab breadcrumbs.
- Behind an experimental setting breadcrumbs.showEditorType (default true).

 Verification steps

 

1. Ensure a file type has multiple editors (e.g. Markdown: text editor + Markdown preview). Open a .md file.
2. The breadcrumbs bar shows a dropdown on the right with the current editor type (e.g. "Text Editor").
3. Click it → menu lists the available editors with the current one checked; picking another reopens the file with it.
4. Use the Set Default submenu → the chosen editor is written to workbench.editorAssociations for .md and becomes the default.
5. Open a .md diff → the dropdown shows "Text Diff Editor"; the Set Default (Diff Only) submenu writes to workbench.diffEditorAssociations; Open Original / Open Modified open each side.
6. Open a plain .txt file (only the default editor) or a file handled by an exclusive editor (Hex) → the dropdown is hidden.
7. Set "breadcrumbs.showEditorType": false → the dropdown disappears; set it back to true → it returns.

I think the recent BYOK utility model change is fixing the wrong layer of the problem.

I understand why silent fallback to Copilot utility models is being changed. If a user selected a BYOK model, hidden Copilot usage can be surprising because it may cross a billing or data boundary. Making that explicit is reasonable.

But making utility model selection mostly global is not the right long-term shape.

One of the things I really like about the current local model support is how simple it can be. For example, with Ollama, I can just pick Ollama from the model/provider setup UI, select a local model, and it appears in VS Code. That simplicity is great. It makes local models feel like a first-class path.

The new utility-model behavior makes that path feel much worse.

A simple local model setup should be:

 choose Ollama as a local model provider
 select an Ollama model as the Agent model
 Agent mode works

It should not become:

 choose Ollama as a local model provider
 select an Ollama model as the Agent model
 start Agent mode
 fail because a separate global small utility model is not configured
 discover another setting
 configure another model
 deal with cold starts, VRAM pressure, or model unload/reload behavior

That failure mode is especially confusing because the user already selected a valid main model. From the user’s point of view, Agent mode should have everything it needs.

For local inference, a “small” utility model is not automatically cheap or fast. The real cost may be loading another model, moving VRAM around, or evicting the model that is already running. In many local setups, the best utility model is simply the currently selected main model.

That is why I think utility routing should follow the selected model or provider.

For example:

 local provider:
 utility model = self
 small utility model = self

 remote BYOK provider:
 utility model = self, provider-specific small model, or Copilot
 small utility model = self, provider-specific small model, or Copilot

 Copilot provider:
 utility model = Copilot utility model

The exact implementation does not matter to me. It could live in the Language Models UI, a provider profile, chatLanguageModels.json, or some other model configuration layer. The important part is that this should not be only one global setting.

A single global chat.utilitySmallModel cannot express normal workflows like:

 when I select a local model, reuse that selected model
 when I select a remote BYOK model, use that provider’s small model
 when I explicitly allow Copilot utility models, use Copilot utility models

Those are different model environments, not just different model names.

I think the default for Ollama/local-style setups should be “self”, or at least there should be an easy way for the provider/model entry to say “use the selected model for utility tasks”.

That preserves the simple local-model setup path that currently makes local/BYOK support feel good in VS Code.

The current global setting feels like a workaround for the immediate error, not the right abstraction.

Please consider making utility model routing configurable per model or per provider, so switching the selected Agent model also switches the effective utility routing.

Related:

- 324007
- 324570
- 324268

Current behavior

Double-click selection appears to be based on generic word separators rather than language tokens.

For example, in JavaScript:

 

Double-clicking may select either 34 or 8 depending on which side of the decimal is clicked, even though 34.8 is a single numeric literal.

The same applies to other numeric forms:

 

 Expected behavior

When language tokenization is available, double-click selection should select the entire language token.

 Why editor.wordSeparators isn't sufficient

Changing word separator behavior globally would also affect unrelated constructs such as:

user.profile.name

where selecting only the clicked identifier is usually the desired behavior.

The editor already recognizes numeric literals as single tokens for syntax highlighting and other language features, so it seems reasonable for double-click selection to use the same token boundaries when available.

This could also benefit other token types where punctuation is part of a single language token (for example, regex literals or CSS color literals), but numeric literals are the clearest and most common example.

<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Current behavior

Double-click selection appears to be based on generic word separators rather than language tokens.

For example, in JavaScript:

```js
const a = 34.8;
```

Double-clicking may select either 34 or 8 depending on which side of the decimal is clicked, even though 34.8 is a single numeric literal.

The same applies to other numeric forms:

```js
1e-6
0xff
0b1010
1_000_000
123n
```

## Expected behavior

When language tokenization is available, double-click selection should select the entire language token.

## Why `editor.wordSeparators` isn't sufficient

Changing word separator behavior globally would also affect unrelated constructs such as:

`user.profile.name`

where selecting only the clicked identifier is usually the desired behavior.

The editor already recognizes numeric literals as single tokens for syntax highlighting and other language features, so it seems reasonable for double-click selection to use the same token boundaries when available.

This could also benefit other token types where punctuation is part of a single language token (for example, regex literals or CSS color literals), but numeric literals are the clearest and most common example.
kept_issues.title: Double-click selection should respect language token boundaries
